rationale: A wins because it keeps the story honest while still making it sharper: “Without the mobile-billing answer, the comparison is not apples to apples” is exactly the caveat that saves the best angle from becoming a correction. B has usable bones, but it decorates the same angle with unsupported scenery like “Epic v. Apple, Substack's 10%, Patreon's tiers,” which is how a decent pitch gets a fact-check rash. A also adds a real fourth lens, “Discord is launching a creator payments business with no earnings data to show for it,” and then has the discipline to say when not to pitch it.
gaps_in_A: “Discord takes 10% where Apple takes 30%” names Apple even though the update only says “30% app-store standard.” It is probably directionally fair, but still an introduced actor.

“The prevailing belief is that a 200-million-user base plus a cheap take rate is an obvious win” is inferred, not evidenced. A admits that, but the line still needs backup before it becomes pitch copy.
The contrarian no-earnings angle is intellectually good but thin as a standalone pitch without beta data, comparable payout data, or a refusal from Discord.
gaps_in_B: “Epic v. Apple, Substack's 10%, Patreon's tiers” imports outside facts and pegs not supplied in the update. That is not context; it is homework the model pretended it had already done.
“Discord, Patreon, Twitch, Geneva” names competitors/platforms not in the facts. A comparison story can ask for comps, but it cannot smuggle them into the angle as established framing.
“Discord servers have historically been free communities” may be true in the real world, but it is not in the supplied update. For this exercise, that is a grounding miss.
The third angle, “Discord opens a paid tier inside community servers built on free membership,” is basically A’s server-owner angle with less bite and less proof discipline.
